title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: One-hot encoding transforms categorical variables into a binary matrix. Each category becomes a column, and rows are filled with 0s and 1s indicating the presence of a category.

title: Columns in the Design Matrix
text: When you one-hot encode the 'sex' column, you create two new columns: $$'sex_{male'}$$ and $$'sex_{female'}$$. Each row will have a $$1$$ in one of these columns and a $$0$$ in the other.

title: Number of Rows in the Design Matrix
text: The number of rows in the design matrix remains the same as the original dataset. Since the dataset has $$20$$ rows, the design matrix will also have $$20$$ rows.
